title: Ghost Arbitration: Mitigating Interconnect Side-Channel Timing Attacks in GPU
problem: Contention for on-chip bandwidth in GPU NoCs enables fine-grain side-channel timing attacks that leak cryptographic key information (RSA bits) and fingerprint kernel execution patterns. Shared interconnect resources allow attackers to extract sensitive information through timing side-channels.
motivation: GPUs widely execute sensitive workloads including cryptographic operations, making them vulnerable to interconnect-based side-channel attacks that can compromise security without specialized privileges.
method: Ghost arbitration tracks phantom requests (when other nodes receive free arbitration slots) to maintain least-recently-used priorities and prevent timing differences visible to attackers. Weighted ghost arbitration further exploits malicious communication patterns to defend against attackers who reverse-engineer the arbitration scheme, preventing information leakage while minimizing performance degradation.
key_novelty: The ghost arbitration mechanism that uses phantom request tracking to hide interconnect contention timing information from attackers while avoiding the severe performance penalties of strict time-division multiplexing.
contributions: Demonstrates practical side-channel attacks extracting RSA key bits and fingerprinting GPU kernels through interconnect contention analysis
Proposes ghost arbitration scheme that prevents contention-based information leakage through phantom request tracking
Introduces weighted ghost arbitration defending against reverse-engineered attacks with minimal performance loss
Achieves 4× performance improvement over strict time-division multiplexing while maintaining security guarantees
limitations: Hardware implementation feasibility, area/power overhead, and applicability to other GPU architectures not discussed.
primary_theme: Secure interconnect arbitration against GPU side-channels
